key_insight: This paper introduces aspect-ratio-adaptive relayout for flowchart-style pipeline figures, so the same method diagram can be cleanly re-edited for papers, slides, posters, and mobile formats without breaking the logic. The goal is not just resizing, but preserving the graph structure and all connections faithfully across canvases.
problem_solved: AI/ML figures often need to be reused across many display formats with very different aspect ratios, which can distort layouts or silently break connections between nodes. This paper addresses the challenge of converting a raster flowchart into a structurally faithful, editable layout that adapts to a target canvas shape.
method: Treats flowchart relayout as a distinct aspect-ratio-adaptive task rather than generic image resizing.
Takes a raster flowchart and a target aspect ratio as input, then reconstructs an editable layout.
Uses an agentic pipeline designed to preserve graph structure and avoid hallucinated connections while relaying out the figure.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes it much easier to repurpose one pipeline figure across papers, slides, posters, and social media without manually redrawing it every time. It helps ensure that method diagrams stay accurate, readable, and publication-ready in every format.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of the same flowchart across multiple aspect ratios
A pipeline diagram showing input raster flowchart -> relayout agent -> editable output
Icons for paper, slides, poster, and phone to show multi-canvas adaptation
Highlighted connection lines/nodes emphasizing structure preservation versus broken layouts
paper_title: One Figure, Every Canvas: Editable Flowchart Relayout via Agentic Pipeline
paper_authors: Shih-Chen Tseng, Chih-Hsuan Chen, Ryan Yang, Hsi-An Chen, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu
